Lemma
[A Scalar Product Has Trivial Radical]

↗ lem:nondegenerate-symmetric-bilinear

The radical of a scalar product $q$ is $\{ 0\} $; explicitly, if $q(v,v)=0$ and $w\mapsto q(v,w)+q(w,v)$ vanishes identically, then $v=0$.

Proof

↗ lem:nondegenerate-symmetric-bilinear \sketch Symmetry turns the polar form into $w\mapsto 2q(v,w)$. Its vanishing makes $v$ orthogonal to all of $V$, so nondegeneracy gives $v=0$.

□
